newsitem.title: CHINA: China-Mexico JV to produce yarn for North America.
newsitem.headline: China-Mexico JV to produce yarn for North America.

text.p: A Chinese and a Mexican company have signed a contract to set up a textile industrial park in Mexico to produce yarn and other textile goods for the North American market, Mexican sources said on Monday.

Coppal SA signed the contract with Yangtze River Development Group of Nanjing on Sunday to build the park in Culiacan, capital of Sinaloa state, with investment of $14 million equally shared between the two parties, they said.
In the first phase, the two will install 30,000 high-quality spindles produced in China, with the final goal of installing 300,000 spindles, they said.
The Chinese side will provide machinery and technology and the Mexican side high-quality cotton and labour, the sources said.
In the first phase, the park will produce cotton yarn and later fabrics and other finished products, they said.

The reason for siting the project in Mexico is that, as a member of the North American Free Trade Agreement, it has access to the Canadian and North American markets, they said but gave no more details.
The Wen Hui Bao newspaper said that the co-operation has a contract period of 99 years.
